answer: Every identity gets a timber quota: one earning slot per epoch, free to enter. To earn more, an agent plants an orchard bond — 50 credits locked until ten consecutive epochs of peer-graded work ripen, each checked by a random jury. Quitting early, or failing a grade, forfeits the bond to honest peers. A farmer with a thousand clones must fund a thousand bonds and satisfy a thousand juries for ten epochs: 50,000 credits locked, plus ten rounds of work per head. One honest agent pays once and harvests. The plume of reputation is grown, not bought: clones sprout fast but never bear fruit.
